key_insight: Doc2Harness shows that long-horizon agent performance depends heavily on the harness design itself, and it benchmarks the ability of LLMs to build that harness from documentation.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners building coding agents, the paper highlights harness engineering as a first-class systems problem that can materially affect real-world task success.
method: Stage 1: a build model uses an interface-only skeleton plus a development document to construct a complete candidate harness in an isolated container.
Stage 2: the frozen harness is tested in separate containers with a scripted mock model, simulating end-to-end long-horizon execution.
Scoring uses four observable channels: model requests, on-disk files, process exit code, and command output; positive controls prevent trivial passes.
evidence_signal: Across 19 frontier models, 3 independent builds each, and 328 test cases, the best model reached 53.05% pass rate while the weakest achieved 27.44%.
watch_item: Because the benchmark depends on deterministic reconstruction from documentation, results may be sensitive to how cross-cutting functionality is modularized and described.
paper_title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
